meta.socialDescription: How to start a run club, step by step.

sections.title: How to start a run club
sections.lead: Who it’s for: anyone who runs and wants company for it. It could be a neighbourhood group, a running coach, a café that wants a weekend crowd, or a few friends who keep getting asked “can I join?”

sections.heading: Before the first run
paragraphs: Route. Start and finish at the same place, so nobody has to find their way back. A loop of 3 to 5 km is a friendly start: well lit, few road crossings, easy to describe in one line (“the gate by the lake, the side with the tea stall”). Walk or run it once at the same time of day before you announce it.
Time. In most Indian cities an early weekend start beats the heat and the traffic. Picking a time you can keep every week matters more than finding the perfect slot.
Format. A social run should have room for every pace. Plan two or three pace groups, each with a lead at the front and someone at the back (a “sweep”) so nobody runs alone at the back.
Free or paid. Most social runs are free. Charge when you’re adding something, like a coach, a track session, timing or coffee at the finish.

Sign-up page. Put one link in your bio with the meeting point, start time, distance, the pace groups and what to bring. On {{brand.name}}, runners can give their pace when they book, sign a waiver if you need one, and get a confirmation that tells them where to be.

sections.heading: On the morning
paragraphs: What to get right on the day.
list: Arrival. Be at the meeting point 15 minutes early, somewhere easy to spot. With {{brand.name}}, runners check in by scanning a code at the meeting point, and you can add walk-ins in a few seconds.

Getting people talking. Many newcomers turn up on their own. Before the start, put people into their pace groups and give each group one easy question to answer together. {{brand.name}} builds pace pods from the paces runners gave and gives each pod a first-hello question. While the run is on, it sends runners nothing.

Safety basics. Do a short warm-up and say the route out loud. Name the lead and the sweep. Carry water, a basic first-aid kit and a charged phone. At the finish, count everyone back in. On {{brand.name}}, you or your sweep mark each runner back, and anyone not marked stays on your list until you close the run.

sections.heading: Afterwards
paragraphs: Thank people the same day and say when the next run is. Ask one or two questions about the pace, the route and the time. Pay particular attention to first-timers, because the week after their first run is when they decide whether to come back. {{brand.name}} sends a feedback request after the run to runners on the app, and your report shows who came for the first time and who came back. Every runner also gets their own invite link, so you can see who brings friends.

sections.heading: Checklist
paragraphs: Tick these off before your first one.
list: Route walked at the right time of day
Same meeting point and time, every week
Pace groups, each with a lead and a sweep
Sign-up page with route, time, pace groups and what to bring
Thank-you and next date sent the same day
